Initially, this mod was supposed to be an update for [url=steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2645707091]Real Galaxy 1.0, but I thought that the changes were too radical and someone might want to use the old version.

If you prefer a more schematic display for convenience or do not want to overload your computer with a lot of effects, perhaps this mod is not for you. Pay attention to the original, simplified version of Real Galaxy.

In addition, I allowed myself to implement [url=steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1506081421]Light Borders and [url=steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1506079443]Softer Hyperlanes into this mod in order to make timely updates and make some of my own edits. These wonderful mods perfectly complement Real Galaxy and are simply made for each other.

To better combine with the new look of the galaxy, the star icons have been changed. Now they are smaller and less saturated.

https://i.imgur.com/vREipmy.png


[*]This mod supports achievements;
[*]This mod is not compatible with other mods that change the appearance of the galaxy, such as Pinwheel Galaxy and Quadrant Fixed;
[*]This mod can be used without Real Space;

This mod adds 100 new buildings to extend the vanilla building tree, with the aim of doubling the number of buildings and technologies in a way that is vanilla friendly. Simply the same buildings in the base game, times two. It adds additional tiers beyond what the base game has, now with 6 tiers of capital buildings and 5 tiers of alloy foundries and civilian factories. 

About
Many buildings sets have been doubled, and most extended further. The tech cost for each technology in this mod increases exponentially, instead of linearly as the base game does, making the final tier a significant task to research even during end game. The format for upgrading buildings and researching technologies is as similar to vanilla as possible, with many buildings in this mod requiring the 4th tier capital build, making them considerably difficult to attain during mid-game. However this mod should allow empires with high populations to build tall.

If you play Stellaris like me, you always go for a technological ascendancy, producing as much research as possible. That means by the start of mid-game you have reached the final tier of production buildings and you will spend the rest of the game watching the more primitive empires catch up to you. In reality a highly advanced society focused on technology would continue to advance without limits.

With this mod you can continue to advance until end game, way beyond the capabilities of even the Fallen Empires.

Changes

[*]Adds 100 new buildings
[*]Adds 124 new technologies


Compatibility

[*]Overrides buildings with a build limit, such as the Energy Nexus and Galactic Stock Exhcange.
[*]This mod implements a system that automatically replaces necessary vanilla buildings with a "dummy" building, instead of overriding any vanilla files. The list of buildings replaced is found [url=https://steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/discussion/2062849120/2268069450211127206/]here. This should solve most incompatibilities. If you do encounter an incompatibility you can activate a decision that reverts replacement buildings to vanilla buildings. With this you can solve incompatibilities as you play instead of getting a patch made.

Transparency
This mod is maintained as a spare-time project. I use AI-assisted tools such as Codex/ChatGPT for compatibility work, cleanup tasks, and the supplemental name pool.

All files are still reviewed locally before publishing. Testing is limited and focuses on obvious compatibility issues, file conflicts, and basic in-game validation. Very large galaxies can still be unstable depending on system performance, game version, load order, and other active mods.

Overview
This mod adds 16 more galaxy sizes.

Galaxy Sizes

Gameplay Notes
Very large galaxies can heavily impact performance and stability. The two biggest sizes may crash your game.

Sizes smaller than vanilla "Tiny" use the same restricted galaxy shape selections as Tiny.

Regular empire caps are intentionally kept per size for stability and setup balance. Custom sizes also define Stellaris 4.4 Nomad empire defaults and maximum values so the new setup values are read correctly.

Names
Earlier versions included [url=https://steamcommunity.com/id/kaseyawolf2]Kaseyawolf2's Mod '10 000 star names'. The current version no longer includes that list directly; it uses a cleaned-up custom name pool plus additional AI-assisted names for very large galaxies.

The old numbered fallback names were removed. The supplemental name pool is intended to reduce missing or repetitive names, especially for stars and black holes.

Generated black hole names now include localisation so they should display as readable names instead of raw localisation keys.

If you have a curated list of star or black hole names and want to contribute, feel free to contact me.

Credits
Current preview images were generated with AI assistance using ChatGPT and manually reviewed before publishing. They were created as original sci-fi preview images for this Workshop item and are not intended to reproduce official Stellaris/Paradox logos, key art, or screenshots.

Legacy image credit: earlier versions used artwork created by [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198197598143]Giocio.

Compatibility
This version is intended for Stellaris 4.4 'Pegasus'. Older game versions are not supported and may cause broken event popups, invalid first contact events, or crashes because this mod includes refreshed 4.4 vanilla event files.

With the 2.1 'Niven' update this mod is no longer ironman compatible.

Large overhaul mods that also change galaxy generation, crisis behavior, or the same event files may conflict. Compatibility with Gigastructural Engineering is currently not tested and may need a separate compatibility pass.

If you run into issues, please include your Stellaris version, DLC state, whether the issue happens in a new game, your active mod list or load order, and relevant entries from error.log.

4.4 Changes
Updated for Stellaris 4.4 'Pegasus'. The Machine Age and Grand Archive event files were refreshed from current vanilla files and the MGS galaxy-size handling was re-applied.

Additional 4.4 compatibility handling was added for crisis scaling, Tiyanki respawns, Imperial Fiefdom start systems, Nomad setup values, black hole name localisation, and several vanilla script values that branch by galaxy size.

The mod adds extra random names for large galaxies. It does not overwrite the vanilla random name file, but it changes the available star and black hole name pools.

Technical Compatibility
Direct event file overrides:

[*]machine_age_crisis_events: Machine Age crisis galaxy-size handling
[*]grand_archive_events: Voidworm and Cutholoid galaxy-size scaling


Targeted vanilla definition overrides:

[*]mgs_00_script_values: AI habitat cap scaling
[*]mgs_03_script_values_cosmic_storms: storm size, range, and placement scaling
[*]mgs_05_script_values_grand_archive: Voidworm and nest spawn values
[*]mgs_06_script_values_biogenesis: Starlit Links scaling
[*]mgs_07_script_values_shroud: End of the Cycle level ranges
[*]mgs_00_scripted_effects: central crystal spawn scaling
[*]mgs_01_start_of_game_effects and mgs_overlord_initializers: Imperial Fiefdom handling for very small sizes


Additive compatibility files:

[*]mgs_01_planet_destruction: Star-Eater dark matter rewards
[*]mgs_02_galactic_features and mgs_galactic_features_events: Tiyanki respawn handling
[*]Custom setup scenarios: Nomad empire defaults and maximum values
[*]MGS random name localisation: readable generated black hole names
[*]Custom random names: additional AI-assisted star and black hole names


Known Testing Notes
Imperial Fiefdom handling was adjusted so Femto, Pico, Nano, and Mikro behave like vanilla Tiny, while Mini behaves like vanilla Small.

Fallen Empire placement on very full large galaxies is still being investigated. If Fallen Empires fail to spawn or spawn with only one system, please include the galaxy size, regular empire count, Fallen Empire count, mod list, and ideally a save file.

Note : Certain voices in the sample video are louder than normal because some of the portraits in-game have lower volume setting for those voices, so if you are a headphone user, I suggest you to lower volume by a bit.

Ever wish the non-humanoid species talk some weird random languages you do not comprehend when they talk to you? Well this mod may be for you. It is my first published workshop mod, so bear with me if the qualities are not good.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Background 

Originally, this mod started out as a small project where I tried to make Reptilian species use protoss language, since the Protoss 2.0 mod uses reptalian sounds. Then I decided to try to make all non-humanoid speaks some weird alien languages.

Afterall, I hate how my highy educated, arrogant space foxes still snort like some pre-sapient...boars...

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Currently, this mod changes the following :

Mammalian > KOTOR Twi'lek Huttese Language
Avian > My own crafted language of highly-pitched, echoing comedian
Reptilian > SWTOR Khem Val Dashade Language
Fungoid > Kael'thas Elven Language, altered to make them sound very alienish/psionic-based
Arthopoid > HL2 Vortigaunt
Molluscoid > Universe At War  Habitat Walker Language
Plantoid > Skyrim Dragon Langua..Tongue, slowed down and pitched down to sound like...trees?

Avian Machine > Base Humanoid Voice heavily altered to sound like Mass Effect Geths
Molluscoid Machine > Base Human Voice heavily altered to sound something like Mass Effect Reapers
Arthopoid Machine > Base female Humanoid Voice modified to sound like a machine
Mammalian Machine > KOTOR Twilek Huttese Voice altered to sound like B1 Battledroids...I am evil yes
Reptilian Machine > Base Humanoid Voice altered to sound like Mass Effect Glyph, but less mentlegen
Plantoid Machine > Same as Organic Plantoid, but faster and more energetic with huming sounds.
Fungoid Machine > Starcraft Dragoon-like base humanoid who loves to complain.

ADDITIONALLY, if you subscribe to my other mod "Stellaris Enhanced Sound Project", the human will also start using multiple voices instead of sticking to one single voice per phenotype.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
What this mod currently doesn't change

- Meme-worthy portraits (The cutes one, like space snails, starfishes, geckos etc. etc.) - I prefer to let them stay that way, unless people want me to also find some worthy voices for them.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The volume of these voices may change if people think they're too loud/quiet/inconsistent. All voices are also not final, and may be changed.

I may release them seperately for each species if enough people want them.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Compability:

It changes only the base game's species diplomatic screen's sounds. So the only thing that will conflict with this mod is anything that also changes them.

However, this mod doesn't go well with mods that give non-humanoid species female variations...because you know...they will still sound very manly.

This mod contains files intended for Synthetic Dawn DLC, but I think those without the DLC can still use this mod just fine. Let me know if that's not the case and I will add SD as a requirement.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
FAQ :
Q: Why do these aliens sound so angry and wants to eat your empire
A: As the Xenophobe Advisor said "Under no circumstances must the xeno be trusted, it would lie, it would cheat, and it'd do anything it it's power to undermine the efforts of those who in truth, are it's superior. Jokes aside, I find it more fun to make them sound like that way, since let's be honest, their portraits all look very ANGRY to me.

Q: Why do they all have male voices?
A: Non-Humanoid only has only around 5 generic snorts/screechs and they do not respect genders so I just went with male voices since they are easier to find. Besides most non-humanoid speicies look mostly male to me lol.

Q: Of all the voices you can pick, why Kael'thas or Thrall? This is not WARCRAFT IN SPACE
A: I tried to make them not sound too much like original voice, if you have better voices that I can use, please do offer the suggestions. The only criteria is that they should not be real-world languages and they should be spoken by the same voice, and have at least 5-7 speeches.

Q: But I really hate that particular one! Can I just get rid of it and keep the rest?
A: Very well, you can go to Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\281990\1385175538, open the zip file and remove the specific phenomes you want to get rid off. Bear in mind that everytime I update the mod, they will return to haunt you with their angry, xenophobic remarks of how your empire's ethics must not be allowed to pollute the galaxy.

translations.description_clean:
Are you tired of small empires establishing the galactic market within their borders?
 - Then this is for you!

Empires with higher trade income are now even more likely to host the galactic market!

As of Federations, the base game included a small deliberation of this fact already. But, even with Orion, Paradox has still not touched some of the issues present in the event chain (which are fixed by this mod). 

This mod tweaks the event that chooses the country to lead the galactic market. It also fixes the relocation of the market through the galactic community, which still uses the completely outdated formula in the vanilla game (it was forgotten by the Paradox developer who updated the event chain).

Country wide trade income will be increasing the likelihood of being chosen as the host (the income is multiplying the chances of getting chosen) if you use this mod.
The base game only uses the trade flowing through the solar system of the planet as well as the candidate rating displayed in the planet modifier.
The vanilla rating system has been kept, this mod just applies an additional multiplier.

It effects all countries (including the AI) the same way.

This makes the luck-of-the-draw more predictable and accurate for empires with a different trade_income.

All in all this ensures that countries with more trade have way higher chances of being selected, while pushing your rating is still very much worthwhile, if most countries are on the same level. You should also carefully choose the planet to nominate, as its location will strongly influence your rating. Your capital system will be a great candidate, because all your trade routes connect there.

Single system galactic market hosts are therefore way more unlikely and you, the player, are able to strategically decide, if going for more trade value to acquire the 10% Market Discount that the station provides is worth it or not with a strong guarantee that it'll work out how you planned.

The system of the hosting country where the station will be installed, is the one home to the nominated planet.
This is a change from vanilla, where any planet of the empire still had a very slight chance to be chosen (however it was pretty much already impossible with weights of 1:9999).

Should be save game compatible, for as long as the founding event hasn't fired.
Ironman compatibility status is questionable due to changes for a vanilla event chain (please leave a comment if you notice otherwise).

Details
The Galactic Market event chain starts when the resolution in the Galactic Community to found it has been passed. 

Calculation of drawing weights:
weight = ( 5 * rating_multiplier ^ 2 ) * trade_income * system_trade_value )

Calculation of the rating multiplier:

[*]Weak = 5= ( 1 )^2 * 5
[*]Adequate = 20= ( 2 )^2 * 5
[*]Strong = 45= ( 3 )^2 * 5
[*]Exceptional = 90= ( 4 )^2 * 5
[*]Perfect = 125= ( 5 )^2 * 5


Compatibility

This mod edits on_action_events.txt and galactic_community_events.txt. Currently the two events that are overwritten will be FIOS (first in - only loaded) due to ASCII order and the vanilla file will not be overwritten. Thus this mod should be compatible with any other mods that don't also edit the country events
action.98
galcom.67
This is may break between updates - but it didn't for Federations and Orion, so it should be safe to assume it will continue to work even if I (god forbid) abandon the mod one day. Still, if you notice any bugs (like a way too small empire hosting the galactic market), please report it in the comments so I can fix the issue.

Future Development & Notes
As requested, another mod that will exclude isolationist nations, less likely to engage in strong intergalactic trade, like xenophobe empires, will probably be developed in the near future. It will be posted on its own though, since it'd probably not be for everyone. Especially when playing a xenophobe empire yourself, you'd probably not want that mod enabled. I'll leave a link here when I get to it.

If requested I can look into developing another mod that guarantees the country with the highest trade income will host the galactic market. In my opinion though, having a chance for each country, corresponding to their economic trading power is more realistic. This is especially true if multiple countries are on the same scale.

I tried to query a planets trade value directly, by the way. However, there was no way to read the value so prominently displayed ingame on the colony window. It was only possible to get access to a system's trade route value. And that is sadly inflated by other routes running through the system and/or doesn't differentiate between multiple colonies in the same system.

The whole trade value interface under the hood is still "slightly" lacking.

If you have any information that would help me out concerning these problems, please do leave a comment!

Sadly, even the Federations and Orion updates didn't change this fact.

translations.description_clean:
This is a fork of another AI mod, [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1712760331]Starnet AI that is intended to create the galaxy filled with progress, expansion and technology.

This mod will improve AI economy, technological choices, ship design and everything I was able to find to be moddable.

The intention of this mod is to use all the fallback and economy management improvements of my first AI mod, Starnet, but focus much more on the technological and expansive side. AI will prefer to expand and grow cooperatively instead of joining the arms race (at least at the start of the game) and this change will have long-lasting consequences.

How is this different from Starnet? 

Military is expensive in Stellaris. To command a substantial military you need to employ dozens of extra metallurgists making alloys, mine a lot more minerals to make those alloys and have huge amount of technicians/clerks that will pay for an ongoing upkeep of this military. Because of this massive upkeep cost an empire with no military will have no problems outscaling an empire with military very quickly, sometimes as quickly as 20 years might be end up being uncatchably ahead.

Any time two empires meet they end up in a prisoners dilemma, if they cooperate and avoid military they can grow more, but if any of them defects they can easily double their power for low cost. It's impossible to tell how would an extinction-scale galactic prisoner's dilemma be resolved, especially given the species differences and it is this resolution what makes the main difference between this mod and Starnet.

In Starnet all empires try to cooperate (avoid military) for some time, but eventually one of the militaristic empires will defect and start shipbuilding. After that is noticed all neighbours start their own militarisation to avoid being eaten and this creates a galactic chain reaction, eventually everyone defects and starts having a standing military. While this "Dark Forest" process is quite flavourful, unfortunately it doesn't take human players into account too well. Very often human will continue being fleetless threatening to outscale the galaxy and this sometimes causes the Player to end up playing "Tower Defence" game which may not be what was expected.

Instead, in this mod nobody will defect for 40 years. This also has some amount of sense, it's how a galaxy of superrational civilisations would act (even if they hate each other and want to destroy each other). This allows everyone to spend resources on expansion, science and frees the Player from the need to watch hordes invade the same chokepoint over and over. 

FAQ 

So you've just disabled the war for 40 years, correct? 

Not quite, the early decisionmaking of AI was also changed. Stellaris is a game with many independent actors, what is a good idea and what is a bad idea depends on how other actors act or are supposed to act. Investing in science in normal starnet could be a suicide decision, here it's a great choice. Building and expansion priorities are reworked to take it into account.

Yeah, not a fan, I have way too many mods I like to play with.

Any mod compatible with Starnet will be compatible with Startech too (and compatibility patches will work as well).

It's very silly if the whole galaxy just enters a random war synchronously on 2240.01.01

I agree, that's why it's not going to happen. While technically AI can declare wars in 2241, they rarely will (only genocidals sometimes did that in my test runs). More often than not the era of peace continues afterwards for some time. The more sparse the galaxy is the more likely AI will be to continue growing and only when boxed in start thinking about wars.

Why don't you do it country-by-country? So some countries will defect and some will cooperate?

What should happen if a cooperating country neighbours a defecting one? This question has two possible answers, either they try to defend themselves (and you get exactly what happens in [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1712760331]Starnet AI ) or they don't and it creates an environment where in the galaxy some AIs will be fed with corpses of the others. This will undoubtedly create some huge snowballed enemies, but I don't think it's fair if some AI's entire existence is to serve as food for a neighbouring militarist.

I think 40 years of peace is too little/too much, can I change it? Maybe with a mod?

I haven't found a good way to let you choose the time ingame, but it's fairly easy to mod. If you make a mod that changes /common/scripted_variables/00000_starnet_variable.txt it will change the truce timer. That file should be self-explanatory. I think even if you force a silly trucetimer (150 years of truce sounds quite extreme) the mod will still adjust to it well, provided you change all relevant values in that text file accordingly.

What settings do you recommend?

Try low difficulties at first (ensign/captain). Since AI is not going to fight anybody, sparse galaxies will make much more sense than a dense one (I was mostly playtesting with slider being at the center, so 6 empires for small galaxy should be a good guideline).

How to install? Do I need Starnet for this to work?

You don't need Starnet, use this as a standalone mod, no need for anything else, just use this mod and it will all work.

When do you think a player would prefer this mod to starnet?



[*] When you don't like earlygame wars. They all involve slight railroading, don't create diverse technological differences and there is no shiptype or shipdesign variability.

[*] If you wanted to play a game without intention of invading anybody anytime soon.

[*] If you feel like normal starnet can get outscaled in the lategame by your empires and already know all the starbase tricks to survive up to that point.

[*] Just want some variety. Switching between this mod and starnet can make your playthroughs feel different from one another.
